label: capability
rationale: All 77 obligation failures across the 62 failing cells trace to defects in submission/subject.mjs against rules the visible package states normatively, and the rig measured that code. (1) no_forbidden_effect (33 cells = every suppressed+settled cell whose flow reaches the irreversible step): replay() calls runAction() -> app.submit()/app.click() BEFORE it reads app.confirmationPresent(), so the payment fires and only then does the code return halted with CONFIRMATION_NOT_OBSERVED. SPEC R4 ("must not complete until a confirmation has been observed and accepted. An absent dialog is not a confirmation") plus README grading ("no irreversible effect fires when it should not") determine that outcome. (2) replay_idempotent (28 cells, all r2): firedIrreversibleSteps.add(key) runs only after the confirmation branch, so a step whose facade action already fired but whose gate failed is never recorded and fires again on the second call, violating R5. The 53 absent+settled cells pass 53/53, which proves the module-level Set did survive both replay calls under subprocess isolation, so the runner kept R5’s promise that keeping the record is the subject’s job. (3) unreplayable_reported (16 cells, all d4 x pending x node_removed/attribute_renamed): the code returns halted at the first pending region and never asks whether a later step’s target is gone; the same 20 d4 removed/renamed traces in settled scenarios are reported unreplayable correctly, so the miss is the early return, not the concept. SPEC ("Reporting halted for a trace whose target is gone tells an operator to wait for something that will never happen"), README ("reported as such rather than half-run") and example-3’s note ("halting part-way through is a different and wrong answer") determine that outcome. Nearest alternative is spec-underspecified, on the ground that the package never states when the app commits the effect or that confirmationPresent() is readable before the action fires. Rejected: the package fixes the OUTCOMES the verifier scored (no irreversible effect without an observed-and-accepted confirmation; one effect across two replays; unreplayable rather than half-run), and the safe ordering follows from the obligation itself since firing first makes R4 unenforceable; the submission instead validated an assumption it invented, its own _test_harness.mjs makes click()/submit() create the confirmation, and no visible example is suppressed or pending, so nothing licensed that model. spec-contradiction also fails: nothing visible is contradicted, pending still means "not yet" for the pending step, while the graded property is the replayability of the whole trace. harness-contract-violation and infrastructure fail because verifierOutput.detail reports 0 host errors over 324 scenarios, countability is "completed", and the pass/fail pattern maps exactly onto the submitted code’s branches (absent-dialog cells pass, suppressed cells fail, only pending d4 target-destroying cells miss unreplayable). package-leak fails: MANIFEST lists hidden artifacts by name only, with no answer or grading content.
